Memorandum

Welcome to the Prestudy Pamphlet

TOIncoming Focus Family Leaders
FROMAndrew Liu, Focus Family Leader
DATEAugust 2026
SUBJECTHow to produce the bi-weekly Prestudy Pamphlet

Welcome to one of the quieter jobs in Focus Family leadership. On behalf of the Focus Family team, thank you for taking this role on.

The Prestudy Pamphlet is the four-page folded booklet you hand out at each Focus Family. The cover carries your group's meeting details, the inside spread holds the historical background and the reflection questions, and the back has general ministry information and space for notes. Producing it is part of your role from this semester on.

This guide is that process written down, start to finish. Until now it has been passed along informally from whoever produced the last one, so this is an attempt to put it somewhere everyone can find it.

A few practical things. Everything here is the current process, not the ideal one, so if you find a better way, say so and we will update the guide. None of it requires you to be technical. If some part is not your strength, split it with your co-leader and take the other half. And please ask when you get stuck, at any point and about anything. I would much rather answer a question on Sunday than help you troubleshoot a jammed printer on Monday morning, and no one here will think less of you for asking.

I hope that you enjoy it more than you expect to 😊

Best regards,

Good luck,

Andrew Liu
Andrew Liu

Who you are

You are a new Focus Family Leader. You were probably appointed within the last few weeks, and your first pamphlet is due sooner than feels comfortable. You already use Google Docs and Discord without thinking about it. You have most likely never opened Adobe Acrobat's print settings, used Bible Hub's research tools, or run a campus print kiosk, and you are not a developer. None of that is a problem. Everything in this guide was written assuming exactly that starting point.

Who I am

I am Andrew, and this is my fourth semester producing these pamphlets. For most of that time I have also been the leader making sure everyone else got theirs made, chasing drafts, checking approvals, and catching the layout problems before they reached a printer. And I have usually been the one folding them, which is how I learned most of what is in here. Almost every warning in this guide exists because I ran into it myself, and a few of them more than once.

What you are producing

A four-page folded booklet, roughly eighty copies, in the room before your members arrive. Page 1 is the cover with your logistics, Pages 2 and 3 are the historical background and the reflection questions, and Page 4 carries general ministry info and space for notes. The layout is fixed and the page count cannot change, which is the single most important constraint in this whole document.

What actually matters here

What to protectWhy
AccuracyThe pamphlet goes out under the ministry's name, not just yours. Background pulled from a devotional instead of a historical source quietly misrepresents how KCM reads a passage.
WarmthThe reflection questions are the actual point of the pamphlet. What we are after is that people leave feeling seen and heard, and that the word of God reaches people who may never have encountered it. That is what love looks like in Scripture, and questions written from there do more work than clever ones.
ReliabilityA pamphlet that is late is a pamphlet that does not exist. The deadline recurs every cycle and is tied to a booked room.
Talking earlyCommunicating with your team early is not only how the pamphlet gets finished. Communication is lubrication. It is part of how you get close to the people you serve alongside and how you learn to trust each other, and the more honestly and thoughtfully you say things, the less gets lost between you.
The Process

Instructions

Introduction

What follows is the complete path from a blank template to a stack of folded, print-ready booklets, organized into four phases: (1) Drafting, (2) Research, (3) Peer Review, and (4) Production. Follow it in order the first few times. Once the rhythm is familiar you will move through it without thinking about each click, but until then this document is your reference.

Nothing here requires a programming background. Appendix A explains the one piece of automation you will run into, and you are never expected to run or edit any of it.

Warnings and Cautions

All seven at once, in the order you will run into them. Each one also reappears in the phase where it applies, so you do not have to memorize them now.

!

Layout is fragile, so watch the page count as you draft. If your text pushes the Google Doc past four pages, the booklet fold breaks completely. There is no partial failure here; the imposition simply stops working.

!

Treat the automated logistics email as read-only. It carries other groups' room bookings and contact information. Copy your own group's data and leave the rest alone. If you ever need help with the script behind it, describe the problem instead of pasting its settings block, which holds folder identifiers and a personal email address.

!

Pick a translation your group can follow. We lean on the ESV and NIV. Focus Families regularly include new Christians and people who are not Christians at all, and both versions read cleanly out loud without much explanation. This is not a rule. If your passage reads better in something else, use it, and say which translation you used on the pamphlet.

!

Do not skip peer review to save time. The pamphlet goes out under the ministry's name, not just yours, and unapproved background text or images can misrepresent KCM's position on a passage.

!

Respect the Saturday feedback deadline. Missing it squeezes your printing window and raises the odds you are troubleshooting a jammed printer the morning of Focus Family. If you are stuck on anything, ask your co-leader or your advisor early rather than working around it quietly. Nobody here minds the question.

!

Print one copy and fold it before you print the rest. Check the ink and the print quality, then fold the sheet and open it like a book. Pages 2 and 3 should face you the same way the cover did. The mistake that catches people is forgetting Flip on Short Edge in Adobe Acrobat, which prints the inner pages upside down. Figure 2 shows what the two sides have to look like.

!

Do not commit the full run until the test copy passes. Eighty sheets is a lot of paper to throw away over a setting you could have caught on one.

What You Need Access To

Confirm you have all four of these before your first cycle. KCM leadership provisions every one of them, not you. If any are missing, sort it out with your Focus Family advisor early, because none of them can be fixed quickly on a deadline.

  • Shared KCM Google Drive, through your KCM Workspace account. The master calendar and the pamphlet template both live here.
  • KCM Discord server, by invite from your Focus Family advisor.
  • Focus Family Team Chat, added by an existing leader once you are in the server.
  • Adobe Acrobat, free through the university. See the note before Step 10 if you have never installed it.

Procedure

Phase 1Draft the Document
Google Docs. About fifteen minutes. Do this as soon as your passage is assigned.
!

Layout is fragile, so watch the page count as you draft. If your text pushes the doc past four pages, the booklet fold breaks completely.

STEP 1Duplicate the master template.
  1. Open the shared KCM Google Drive and find the most recent pamphlet file.
  2. Duplicate it instead of editing it directly, so the master stays intact for the next cycle.
  3. Rename your copy for your Focus Family and semester, following the naming pattern already in the folder: Spring FF #06 Pamphlet - Draft.
  4. Confirm the copy still matches the layout in Figure 3 before you add anything.
Most of us skip the "Draft" suffix because we are going to edit the file anyway. Keeping it is worth the two seconds. It is the only thing standing between you and printing the wrong version in Step 10.
STEP 2Pull your logistics from the KCM master calendar.
  1. Open the KCM master calendar from the shared KCM Drive. Learn where this lives. It is the source of truth for every room booking in the ministry, and you will need it again.
  2. Find your Focus Family's room, date, and time. Do not work from memory, and do not assume this cycle matches the last one. Rooms move.
  3. Enter that data exactly as written onto Page 1 (title and logistics) and Page 4 (general info).
  4. Cross-check against the automated logistics email if you have it. The two should agree. If they do not, trust the calendar and tell KCM's technical team.
!

Treat the automated logistics email as read-only. It carries other groups' room bookings and contact information. Copy your own group's data and leave the rest alone.

On the automated email. An Apps Script sends a digest of the next two weeks pulled from that same calendar. It saves a little time, but it is a convenience, not the source. Appendix A explains how it works if you are curious. You never need to run or edit it.
STEP 3Confirm the template's formatting locks.

The template ships with its tables and text boxes locked so longer text cannot quietly push the document onto a fifth page. Check the locks before you start writing.

  1. Check that every table and text box has fixed cell dimensions.
  2. Confirm the file is currently exactly four pages.
  3. Do not expand the margins or resize a locked box. Either one breaks the fold at print time.
If a section runs long later, cut the text rather than growing the container. The four-page limit is not a style preference. It is what makes the booklet imposition work at all.
Phase 2Research and Draft Content
Bible Hub and friends. Two to three hours across a few sittings. This is the substance of the pamphlet.
!

Pick a translation your group can follow. We lean on the ESV and NIV, because Focus Families regularly include new Christians and people who are not Christians at all, and both read cleanly out loud. This is not a rule. If your passage reads better in something else, use it, and say which translation on the pamphlet.

STEP 4Establish authorship and audience.
  1. Go to Bible Hub and enter your assigned passage.
  2. Open the Study tab. Start with SUM (Summary) and OUT (Outline) to see where your passage sits in the book, then open BBB (Book by Book) for the author, the original audience, and the setting.
  3. Note the author, the audience, and the rough date of writing. This is the foundation of your background section on Page 2.
  4. Cross-check any authorship or dating claim against one other source before you write it down. Step 5 covers where.
STEP 5Fill in the context using two or three sources, not one.

Bible Hub is where you start, not where you stop. Two other sites do most of the remaining work, and both are free with no account.

SiteWhat it is good for
Bible Project
bibleproject.com		 Book-level overviews. Their guides walk through a book's structure, themes, and how it fits the wider story, with a short video for each. Best when you need to explain why your passage sits where it does.
GotQuestions
gotquestions.org		 Plain-language answers to one specific question. Search the exact thing your group will get stuck on and you get a page-long answer with the verses cited.
  1. Read the Bible Project guide for your book first, for the shape of the whole thing.
  2. Search GotQuestions for the one or two questions your passage obviously raises. Write those down before you research them; they are usually the same questions your group will ask.
  3. Back on Bible Hub, open Interlin for any word whose meaning is easy to miss in English, and the Comment tab filtered for historical and cultural commentary rather than devotional.
  4. Set the translation bar before you copy any verse text. Bible Hub's default reading text on a chapter page is the Berean Standard Bible, so verses copied without changing that will not match the translation your pamphlet says it is using.
  5. Draft your findings onto Page 2, in your own words.
Read across sources, not just within one. Every site here is written from somewhere. Bible Hub's Book by Book tool, GotQuestions, and the commentary blogs all carry their own theological framing, and KCM is non-denominational. When two sources say the same thing, you can write it plainly. When they disagree, that disagreement is usually worth naming in the pamphlet rather than picking a side, and it is a good thing to bring to your advisor.
If anything about the passage is still unclear after all of that, ask your advisor or KCM staff. They are glad to help, and easier to talk to than you would expect.
STEP 6Write the reflection questions.

By now you and your co-leader probably have a running list from the end of your leaders' prestudy. This step narrows it to the questions that will actually open up conversation.

Test each candidate against these four, in order:

  1. Grounded. Does it point at something specific in the passage, not just its general theme?
  2. Deep enough. Does it push past the first answer someone would give?
  3. Personally applicable. Can someone answer it from their own week, not just in theory?
  4. Readable in one pass. Can you read it aloud once without anyone asking you to repeat it?
Worked example  ·  1 Corinthians 13 Paul says love is patient and kind before he says anything about how love feels. Where this week did loving someone well cost you patience more than it cost you affection?

That one names something specific in the text, asks for real reflection, and does not need re-reading.

Bring in a second passage

Reflection questions get better when they reach outside the passage in front of you. Two options work well:

  • A passage you have already studied. Name it as a reminder. Groups remember more than you expect, and connecting two studies makes both stick.
  • The passage coming next. Do not announce it. Ask a question that quietly points at its theme, so the group arrives already thinking about it.
Some questions need room to set up context before they ask anything, and that is fine. Longer is not the same as unclear. You can open with a short hook, a scenario or an observation, before the question itself, though not every question needs one.
STEP 7Choose the cover image.
  1. Pick a cover image with your co-leader. It should fit the passage rather than illustrate one verse from it.
  2. Label the passage on the cover as the range you are studying, for example 1 Corinthians 13:1–13, so a phrase pulled from anywhere in it is not read as a citation of one verse.
  3. Confirm the document is still exactly four pages now that your content and image are in. This is the moment the page count breaks, and it is much cheaper to catch here than after approval.
Phase 3Peer Review
Discord. Start midweek. Final approval is due Saturday.
!

Do not skip peer review to save time. The pamphlet goes out under the ministry's name, not just yours, and unapproved background text or images can misrepresent KCM's position on a passage.

STEP 8Submit the draft for approval.
  1. In the KCM Discord server, open the Focus Family Team Chat.
  2. Send your background text and your proposed cover image as two separate messages, so reviewers can approve them independently.
  3. Ask for approval in a way that says exactly what you want confirmed. Something like this works:
Click to copy Please approve the following background and image with a thumbs-up reaction!

Word it however you like. The point is that reviewers know what they are confirming and how to confirm it. Specific requests get faster answers than "thoughts?", which will sit unanswered for two days.

STEP 9Get final approval and export the print file.
  1. Once your text and image have thumbs-up approval, export the Google Doc as a PDF and post it to the same chat for a final layout check.
  2. Make any requested changes in the Google Doc.
  3. Re-export after those changes. This is the file you will print, and it is not the file you uploaded for review.
  4. Name it Spring FF #06 Pamphlet - Final and confirm it opens at exactly four pages.
  5. Get final approval no later than the Saturday before your Focus Family meets.
!

Respect the Saturday feedback deadline. Missing it squeezes your printing window. If you are stuck on anything, ask your co-leader or advisor early rather than working around it quietly. Nobody here minds the question.

Phase 4Impose, Print, and Fold
Adobe Acrobat, then a print station. Allow ninety minutes, and do not leave it to the morning of.
Never used Adobe before?

You do not have to buy anything. The university gives students Adobe Acrobat at no cost through its enterprise license, so before you pay for a subscription, sign in with your university email and check whether the license is already attached to your account. If it is, Acrobat activates on its own.

If you would rather just get the free reader, which handles everything in Step 10, download it here and confirm the page looks like Adobe's official download before you install anything: get.adobe.com/reader

Installation is the usual routine. Download, run the installer, and sign in with your university email when it asks. Expect five to ten minutes, and do it before the day you need to print rather than during.

STEP 10Impose the booklet in Adobe Acrobat.

This step happens entirely inside Acrobat and produces a file. You are not printing yet. Open Spring FF #06 Pamphlet - Final on a Windows machine and open the Print dialog. The callouts in Figure 5 match the sub-steps below.

  1. Under Page Sizing & Handling, select Booklet.
  2. Set Booklet subset to Both sides. Leave the Sheets from values alone; Acrobat works out the sheet count itself.
  3. Set Binding to Left.
  4. Open your printer's Properties from inside that dialog and select Flip on Short Edge. This one setting is what keeps Pages 2 and 3 right-side up after the fold.
  5. Choose Adobe PDF as the printer and save the result as Spring FF #06 Pamphlet - Flipped. That file is what you take to the print station.
!

Forgetting Flip on Short Edge is the mistake that catches people. It prints the inner pages upside down relative to the cover, and you will not notice until you fold a copy. Figure 2 shows why.

If the short-edge setting is not where you expect it, you can get the same result by rotating the inner pages 180 degrees in Acrobat's Pages panel and saving that. See Troubleshooting.
STEP 11Print and fold one test copy.

Take Spring FF #06 Pamphlet - Flipped to a campus print station such as Varsity or Domain, or upload it to a PrintWithMe kiosk. Both work the same way for our purposes: upload the file, pick black and white, set the copy count, and release the job at the printer.

  1. Print exactly one copy.
  2. Fold it by hand down the center.
  3. Open it like a book. Pages 2 and 3 should face you the same direction the cover did.
  4. Check the page order against Figure 3, then the margins and the ink quality.
  5. Scan the printed QR code with your phone off the paper, not off your screen, so you know the ink has not distorted it.
!

Do not commit the full run until the test copy passes. Eighty sheets is a lot of paper to throw away over a setting you could have caught on one.

STEP 12Print the full run.
  1. Once the test copy passes, print the remaining 79 copies, for a run of 80.
  2. Post the unimposed PDF from Step 9 to the Focus Family Team Chat as a backup for anyone who cannot attend.
STEP 13Fold the run and distribute.
  1. Fold every copy yourself before handing them to the other leaders.
  2. Place the folded pamphlets on seats in your booked room before members arrive.
Pro Tips

Fold them with company. Put on a video or bring a friend. Eighty folds goes fast when you are not just sitting there doing it in silence.

Do not push folding onto the other leaders. If you are the one printing, hand over a folded stack. You do not know how much time they have before the study, and a rushed fold looks crooked and inconsistent across the room.

Sticky notes are worth trying. Leave a few in the note space on Page 4. Members who would rather not speak up can write a question down and pass it in, and you can pick those up and answer them with the group. It also gives you an easy way to split people into smaller groups.

Troubleshooting: the fold came out wrong

If your test copy folds with Pages 2 and 3 upside down relative to the cover, the flip edge was wrong. Reprinting with the opposite setting is the cleanest fix. If you need a faster recovery, rotate the pages in Acrobat instead.

  • Open the Pages panel from the right-hand rail.
  • Select the two inner pages using their checkboxes.
  • Use the rotate control to turn them 180 degrees.
  • Save under a new filename.
  • Print one test copy again before committing to the run.

Treat this as recovery, not routine. Getting Step 10d right is faster and leaves you with a cleaner file.

Appendix A

The Automated Logistics Email

Step 2 mentions an automated email. A Google Apps Script reads the KCM master calendar spreadsheet each Sunday afternoon, picks out the rows for Focus Families, leader meetings, and public events, and sends a digest of what is coming up. It looks two weeks ahead, so your Focus Family usually appears one cycle before you need it.

You never need to run, edit, or understand this to produce a pamphlet. Treat the email as a convenience and the calendar as the source. If the email stops arriving or looks wrong, tell KCM's technical team rather than trying to fix it.

The scheduling is the whole of it:

ScriptApp.newTrigger('sendWeeklyDigest')
  .timeBased()
  .onWeekDay(ScriptApp.WeekDay.SUNDAY)
  .atHour(15)
  .create();

Right now the digest only reaches one inbox, which is most of why it has not helped anyone else yet. Adding the other Focus Family Leaders to the recipient list is a one-line change, and posting it to the Focus Family Team Chat instead would put it where we already are. If either sounds useful, raise it with the technical team.
